newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Chemapol to buy into local TV - agency.
newsitem.headline: Czech Chemapol to buy into local TV - agency.

text.p: Czech chemical concern Chemapol Group a.s. is planning to acquire a 50 percent stake in a group of regional Czech TV broadcasters RTS a.s., the news agency CTK reported on Wednesday.
CTK quoted Ivo Brabec, the director of RTS, based in the second Czech city of Brno, as saying that the transaction would be completed within a month.
No more details of the sale were disclosed.
Chemapol Spokesman Miroslav Jilek declined to comment on the report, and RTS officials were not immediately available for comment.
RTS broadcasts three hours daily from four regional studios on the private station TV Prima.

CTK quoted Brabec as saying that five more regional TV stations would join RTS this summer, bringing the total number of viewers reached by its signal to seven million, some 70 percent of the country's population.
Chemapol has been attempting to add a television station to its diverse holdings which range from a number of chemical, engineering and arms trading companies to petrol distribution and real estate.
Jilek told Reuters that Chemapol was still interested in buying into Prima TV, which is controlled by bank IPB.

Prima is the second private channel in the Czech Republic but has been fighting large losses and a tiny audience while its main competitor, TV Nova, owned by Central European Media Enterprises Ltd, has thrived.
